## Academic context

This report presents selected analyses from the 2024–2025 Mathematics thesis
*Modelos estadísticos de tipo self-exciting*. It examines temporal clustering in
Chicago Bulls made field goals, excluding free throws.

## Data and model

```{r data}
data <- scoring_data()
baskets <- as.data.frame(data)
knitr::kable(data.frame(games = nrow(data$games), field_goals = nrow(baskets),
  two_pointers = sum(baskets$tipo == "2"), three_pointers = sum(baskets$tipo == "3")))
```

The intensity is $\lambda(t)=\mu+\sum_{t_i<t}\theta e^{-\phi(t-t_i)}$.
The history restarts for each game. DEoptim retains the bounds $(0,0,0)$ to
$(2,2,100)$ and 1,000 iterations. Individual comparisons use the original
midpoint sum; the joint fit uses the original trapezoid convention.

## Historical reference values

These are transcribed values, not recalculations. The thesis and archived HTML
remain separate sources where their values disagree.

```{r references}
reference <- read.csv("results/reference/selected_results.csv")
reference$source <- ifelse(reference$source == "TFG_memoria.pdf", "Thesis", "Archived HTML")
view <- reference[c("case", "method", "source", "mu", "theta", "phi", "negative_log_likelihood")]
names(view) <- c("Case", "Method", "Source", "mu", "theta", "phi", "NLL")
knitr::kable(view, digits = 6)
```

## Selected-game estimates

The reported NLL re-evaluates both parameter estimates using the same historical
midpoint sum. It is not stelfi's internal objective; that value is stored
separately in the CSV. The default stelfi model imposes theta < phi, whereas
DEoptim uses the original box bounds without that constraint. The results
therefore do not constitute a controlled comparison of optimizers.

```{r selected}
path <- "results/reproduced/comparison.csv"
if (!file.exists(path)) path <- "results/reproduced/selected_deoptim.csv"
if (file.exists(path)) {
  estimates <- read.csv(path)
  view <- estimates[c("case", "method", "mu", "theta", "phi", "negative_log_likelihood")]
  names(view) <- c("Case", "Method", "mu", "theta", "phi", "Scored NLL")
  knitr::kable(view, digits = 6)
} else cat("Run the selected-game fitting scripts to generate this table.")
```

```{r plots, fig.width=8, fig.height=5.5}
paths <- file.path("results/reproduced", c("deoptim_fits.rds", "stelfi_fits.rds"))
if (file.exists(paths[1])) {
  deoptim <- readRDS(paths[1])
  stelfi <- if (file.exists(paths[2])) readRDS(paths[2]) else NULL
  for (name in names(deoptim)) {
    if (!is.null(stelfi)) {
      limits <- comparison_limits(deoptim[[name]], stelfi[[name]])
      plot(deoptim[[name]], ylim = limits)
      plot(stelfi[[name]], ylim = limits)
    } else plot(deoptim[[name]])
  }
}
```

Both methods use the same vertical range for each game, starting at zero.
Rendering this report reads saved fit objects and does not rerun optimization.

```{r season}
path <- "results/reproduced/team_season.csv"
```

## Warnings and interpretation

```{r warnings}
path <- "results/reproduced/stelfi_warnings.csv"
if (file.exists(path)) {
  recorded <- read.csv(path)
  if (nrow(recorded)) knitr::kable(recorded)
}
```

The covariance warning limits uncertainty interpretation for the affected fit.
Finite point estimates are retained; no confidence interval is inferred from an
invalid covariance calculation. Stelfi 1.0.1 does not retain its optimizer's
convergence flag, so completion is not reported as proof of convergence.

The thesis describes clustering in selected games and a near-zero team excitation
estimate across the supplied season. These temporal patterns do not isolate a
causal hot-hand effect. Court time and shot opportunities are not modelled;
historical player windows may be truncated. Phi is poorly identified near
theta = 0. The highlighted-game joint selections and confidence intervals remain
outside this executable subset because their provenance is incomplete.
